title: Traffic shadowing and surge linearization for dedicated capacity: long-window throughput stitching and tail-latency fingerprinting
creator: Marco Diaz
description: Objective: validate Dedicated capacity autoscaling and runtime behavior under realistic, long-duration workloads that combine steady baseline traffic with intermittent high-frequency surges. Create a reusable harness that can: 1) shadow production requests into an isolated Dedicated test pool without impacting production, 2) stitch together realistic token/sec distributions over 72+ hour windows, and 3) produce fingerprinted tail-latency profiles (p50/p95/p99) for regression detection and alerting. This ticket covers design, infra changes for safe shadowing, load generator updates, dashboards/alerts, and an initial 72-hour run matrix.
acceptance_criteria: - Shadowed traffic pipeline deployed to dedicated test pool and gated by header-based opt-in so production unaffected.
test_plan: 1) Build shadowing proxy that strips credentials, adds test header, and forwards copies to a dedicated cluster. 2) Implement sequence-length-aware sampler and token-STS (tokens/sec) replay engine to reproduce burst+steady distributions. 3) Execute a 72-hour run per scenario (baseline-only, baseline+2x surrogate bursts, baseline+10x microbursts) capturing per-route tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, error-rate, kernel-warmup time, and scale events. 4) Run regression detector daily comparing latest fingerprint against baseline snapshot. 5) Capture full KV-cache hit curves and cold-start tails. Logs and traces written to s3 for offline analysis.
design_decisions:
- Use non-production credentials and header flag 'X-RI-Shadow: true' to prevent side-effects.
- Shadow copies are syntheticized: request bodies are scrubbed and user-identifiers hashed.
- Use a two-stage generator: steady-state Poisson traffic for baseline + superimposed Markovian bursts for microburst realism.
- Introduce a warm-pool prefetch step (warm up GPUs with no-op prompts) to measure startup delta vs no-warm-pool.
- Prefer token-level instrumentation (tokens/sec) over request/sec to reflect LLM cost/throughput.
observations:
- Initial 24h run showed autoscaler undershoot on 5x microbursts due to container startup latency; p95 spiked to ~1.1s for short bursts.
- After enabling a small warm pool and bumping the scale cooldown window, p95 tail reduced ~28% during bursts.
- KV cache priming via prefix replay reduced token churn for repeated prefixes; p99 improvements were most visible on long-context requests.
- One regression flagged: a recent kernel selection change increased steady-state p95 by ~60ms for medium-length inputs (tracked to quantized matmul fallback path).
next_steps:
- Instrument autoscaler to expose 'scale_decision_latency' metric and add to dashboard.
- Run full 72-hour matrix with warm-pool sizes [0,2,6] and burst multipliers [2x,5x,10x].
- Add automated nightly fingerprint comparison job and a PR-driven baseline update flow.
- Create runbook entry for investigating p95 regressions with checklist: reproduce with isolated generator, gather traces, bisect runtime/quantization change, rollback if necessary.
